sourceNote: Burger King Deutschland's Nährwerte & Allergene page (https://www.burgerking.de/naehrwerte_allergene) publishes no table: it sends readers to each product under Menü, where "Lebensmittelinformationen inkl. Allergenen und Nährwerte" shows the values per 100 g/100 ml and per portion with the portion size, and the allergens; the page says the values come from its suppliers' food analyses, apply to Germany only, and that not every product is sold in every restaurant. The menu page (https://www.burgerking.de/menu) and the product pages read them from the site's own content service, Sanity dataset prod_bk_de at czqk28jt.apicdn.sanity.io (the page asks it per product with the GraphQL operation GetItem); each row records that service's public query for the item as dataURL and the SHA-256 of its result. The service also states fibre per portion and per 100 g, which the page table does not show; the file keeps it as the chain's own figure. For drinks the table's 100 g/100 ml column is per 100 ml and the portion figure is the sold volume; the file keeps the figures as stated (servingGrams is that figure, servingUnit ml). A per-100 value the service leaves empty is derived from the portion value and the stated portion weight. Where a stated per-100 value contradicts the portion's own figure, kJ against kcal decides the energy, the energy decides fat, carbohydrate and protein, and fibre, sugar, saturated fat and salt follow the side the energy chose or are left out when nothing decides; a row whose energy no check settles is left out. The energy must then fit the macronutrients (9 kcal per g fat, 4 per g carbohydrate and protein, 2 per g fibre, within 20 % or 12 kcal); a fibre figure that alone breaks the fit is left out, and a row that still does not fit is left out. Each such row says so in valueNotes. portionMilliliters is set where the chain states the volume, in the name or, for the King Shakes, in the description.
sha256Note: SHA-256 over the per-row sha256 values concatenated in ascending item id; each row sha256 is the SHA-256 of the query result as compact JSON with sorted keys (the response itself carries a timing field that changes per request).
